$comment: Explicit, versioned opt-outs for scripts/breaking_schema_check.py (an ENFORCE, blocking gate). The gate's rule is not 'you may not break the contract' — it is 'you may not break it silently'. A change stays allowed; the silence does not. An entry only grants an opt-out when file, rule, reason, and version are all present, AND reason is real prose explaining WHY the tightening is intentional and reviewed — a bare issue/PR reference, 'TODO', 'see PR', or anything under ~20 chars / a single word is rejected (see reason_rejection()). pointer_prefix is optional and defaults to matching every finding for that rule in that file; add it to scope a narrower, single-field opt-out instead. Entries do not expire — a bound-hardening acknowledgement is a permanent historical fact about that contract, not a lease.

entries.reason: EvidenceCase is an intentional coordinated response expansion. Pinning TraigentBackend to this Schema revision before planner emission is necessary but not sufficient: rollout remains blocked until every strict or generated response consumer is reconciled with evidence_case.

This intentionally expands the governed extension vocabulary so schemas can declare mechanically checked cross-field equality. It is contract mechanics only, and consumers of the closed registry must update for the new property.

Registers the Agent Lifecycle Record Part 1 client-boundary disclosure annotation (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:376-408) in the governed x-* extension vocabulary so agent_lifecycle_record/*.json schemas can carry it, matching the existing x-traigent-invariants precedent immediately above. This file is documentation/governance metadata only -- its own header states it is 'not applied as a JSON Schema validator over other schemas' -- so no real request or response payload is ever validated against x_extensions_meta_schema.json itself; the breaking-check finding is the generic conservative heuristic correctly erring cautious on a bare-named resource file, not evidence of an actual wire-consumer break. Unlocks contract mutation row 17 (PART1_CONTRACT_FREEZE_DRAFT.md:1155), one of the five Schema-owned mutations Internal Contract Freeze requires to be executable.

identity_state is an explicit discriminator when present, with a closed enum of identified/unidentified and a strictly validated absent/legacy migration branch (expand-contract); rollout stays flag-off until Backend and strict consumers emit and handle it.
agent_id is nullable only in the unidentified branch, with paired-null invariants, because inventing an agent would corrupt provenance; identified rows remain string-valued.

Expand-contract: identity_state is dropped from the top-level required list because the active Backend does not yet emit it on every experiment-group item or provenance row. The enum stays closed to identified/unidentified only; absence is handled by a new, strictly validated legacy branch (string agent_id, string-or-null dataset_id, no run_id), never treated as identified or as a certified explicit-none dataset claim. A follow-up MAJOR revision re-tightens this back to required once the Backend backfills the field everywhere.

The allOf branch count on ExperimentGroupOverview goes from 3 to 4 and on GroupedConfigurationRunProvenance goes from 2 to 3 because a new, absence-only branch was added alongside the existing identified/unidentified branches to enforce the legacy no-identity_state shape structurally (string agent_id, string-or-null dataset_id, run_id null-or-absent). The pre-existing branches on each definition are unchanged; the new branch only tightens validation for the newly-optional legacy case, it does not loosen any previously-enforced constraint.

Retires the subtractive curation vocabulary at the client boundary (#389). `remove_redundant` is removed from the enum because acting on subtractive advice keyed to an observed signal biases the customer's own measurement and is unrepairable -- excluded items carry zero inclusion probability. Measured on a 70-item confirmation set, top-15-by-observed-discrimination pruning gave -0.202 against a true -0.073 (2.77x); random-15 was unbiased at -0.078. Breaking is the intended effect: a consumer still emitting or matching this member must be reconciled rather than silently accepted. Recorded in the disclosure register; reintroducing a subtractive category needs an owner decision. Scoped by pointer_prefix to the one enum that actually carried the retired member: an entry with no prefix defaults to matching every enum finding in the file forever (find_allow_entry uses startswith on an empty string), which would silently pre-authorize unrelated future enum breaks.
